Eva Perón. Known as Evita, she was an Argentine actress and wife of Juan Perón who became a powerful political figure in her own right. She championed workers' rights and social welfare, becoming a beloved symbol of Peronism and Argentine nationalism before her death from cancer at age thirty-three.

Eva rose from poverty in rural Argentina to become a radio and film actress before marrying Juan Perón in 1945. Once in power, she created the Eva Perón Foundation, which distributed money and aid to Argentina's poor, funding schools, hospitals, and housing. She campaigned for women's suffrage and universal voting rights, which were granted in 1947 under her influence. The government earned her the title Spiritual Leader of the Nation, and she maintained immense popularity despite lacking formal governmental power. After her death, her embalmed body was publicly displayed, and she became an iconic figure in Argentine culture and politics. Her life inspired the musical Evita by Andrew Lloyd Webber, cementing her status as a global cultural icon.
